messages:
maria: Heads up — support ticket (ACME) reporting p99 regressions since ~10:05am after the recent routing change. p95 ~420ms (baseline ~180ms), p99 ~1.3s.

leo-support: Customer correlated spike with bursts of many short-lived sessions. They sent request headers that include a session token in the 'x-user-prefix' header. :frowning:

jia: Looking at metrics — KV prefix cache miss rate jumped ~6x at the same time, and eviction rate spiked. Hotshard eviction count doubled. Heatmap shows a very high prefix-cardinality.

oncall-bot: Alert: service/inference latency_p99 > 1s for 12m (rule: latency_p99 > 1s)

sam: Quick triage notes: no obvious regressions in kernel selection. Suspect cache key variance. Can someone try a quick synthetic to reproduce?

leo-support: Repro steps from the customer (sanitized):
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 5000); do
  curl -s -H "x-user-prefix: user-$(uuidgen)-session" \
    -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
```
This rapidly creates 5k unique prefixes and correlates with their spike.

jia: Ran a focused repro in staging with that loop. Confirmed cache miss/eviction pattern. Root cause hypothesis: key normalization bug — we were not stripping ephemeral session tokens from the prefix normalization path in the recent header-parsing refactor, so cache keys include high-entropy tokens.

maria: Nice catch. That would massively increase cardinality and cause constant churn + warmup penalties. Any quick mitigations?

sam: Short-term mitigations to reduce customer pain:
- enable prefix-key hashing fallback (feature flag) so similar prefixes map to same canonical bucket
- increase local KV cache size per shard + raise eviction_threshold temporarily
- add an admission circuit: if prefix_entropy > threshold, bypass KV cache for that request (and log tag)

leo-support: I can patch the support response: suggest they stop sending ephemeral tokens in prefix header and provide a code snippet to use stable prefix keys. Also offer a temporary routing rule to throttle their burst rate.

jia: I pushed a quick fix branch that strips tokens matching the session regex in the normalization function and adds unit tests. Also adding a metric for prefix_entropy and a histogram for key_length. PR: https://git.internal/r/PR-4321

maria: Plan: roll the normalization fix to a small canary, enable hashing fallback and circuit-breaker as an ops knob. Monitor p95/p99 + eviction rate. If canary looks good, promote. Communicate ETA to support.

ops-bot: Deploy started: deploy/eng-runtime/canary-3-nodes (maria initiated)

jia: Canary results after 30m: p95 down ~35%, p99 down ~50% in the canary pool. Eviction rate back to baseline. Prefix_entropy metric dip visible.

sam: Added a temporary SLO override to avoid cascading alerts while we stabilize. Also opened a follow-up ticket to add synthetic warmup scripts for high-cardinality workloads and to build a test harness that simulates prefix entropy.

maria: Support informed, customer accepted workaround and will change header usage in their SDK. We'll schedule a short postmortem and add test coverage + lint rules preventing including ephemeral tokens in prefix headers.

leo-support: I'll send the customer the recommended SDK snippet and timeline.

jia: Follow-ups: revert the temporary cache size bump after one week unless telemetry suggests otherwise, and add the prefix_entropy alert with a runbook.

maria: Closing loop for now. Big win: patch + canary removed the p99 spikes. Postmortem scheduled for next Tue. Thanks everyone! :tada:
